properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 24 at 6:04AM EDT until October 24 at 6:30AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 nm west of Dry
Tortugas out 60 nm...

* Until 630 AM EDT.

* At 604 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 16 nm southwest of
Tortugas Ecological Reserve South, moving south at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

properties.areaDesc: Ocracoke Island
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 24 at 5:15AM EDT until October 24 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2 feet of inundation above
ground level expected in low- lying areas near shorelines and
tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and low
lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes
adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 1 PM today. Tide levels will continue to
rise with King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-
week. The morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily
tides. King Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 4:03AM AST until October 26 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE... Across the northern coastal areas including western
and eastern coastal areas.

* WHEN...Remains through Saturday afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 2:35AM EDT until October 25 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet
expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Mainland Northern Brevard and
Northern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 11 AM this morning to 8 PM EDT
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 AM Sunday to 8
PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet
expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Mainland Northern Brevard and
Northern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 11 AM this morning to 8 PM EDT
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 AM Sunday to 8
PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 12:42AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.
Relative humidity values are forecast to drop into the low 20 to
mid 30 percent range. The 20 ft wind forecast is expected to
remain at or below 10 mph, which should limit critical fire
weather conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that
may ignite.

Some improvement in humidity levels is expected on Sunday
afternoon with levels about 10 percent higher (30 to 40 percent)
than this afternoon. An additional 10 percent increase is possible
on Monday, which should lower the threat level somewhat.

Numerous local burn bans are in place and continue to expand across
LA and MS due to ongoing drought conditions. This now includes East
Feliciana, Iberville, Pointe Coupee, St. Helena, St Tammany,
Tangipahoa, Washington and West Feliciana Parishes along with
Wilkinson, Amite, Pike, and Walthall Counties. Regardless, outdoor
burning is strongly not recommended this afternoon, and all local
restrictions followed.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS TODAY

feet on 09/06/1909.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, from late Saturday night through Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 23 at 10:45PM MDT until October 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central,
northeast, and southeast New Mexico, including the following areas,
in central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern Lincoln County,
Estancia Valley, Middle Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque
Metro Area, Sandia and Manzano Mountains including Edgewood and
South Central Highlands. In east central New Mexico, De Baca County
and Guadalupe County. In north central New Mexico, Sangre de Cristo
Mountains, Espanola Valley, Far Northwest Highlands, Glorieta Mesa
Including Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains,  Northwest Highlands,
Santa Fe Metro Area, Tusas Mountains Including Chama and Upper Rio
Grande Valley. In northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County,
Far Northeast Highlands, Johnson and Bartlett Mesas Including Raton
Pass and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New Mexico, Chaves
County Plains and Southwest Chaves County.

* WHEN...From 6 AM MDT Saturday through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms will redevelop early Saturday and
expand in coverage though the afternoon. Rainfall rates in excess
of 1 inch per hour may cause flash flooding on already saturated
soils. Arroyos, small streams and channels may quickly rise with
water from heavy rainfall. Repeated rounds of storms will
increase the risk for flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 8:04PM MST until October 25 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall on Wednesday and
Thursday continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST Saturday Night /100 AM MDT Sunday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 750 PM MST /850 PM MDT/, Elevated flow continues near Winslow
to Leupp. Elevated flow is forecast to continue through at least
Saturday evening.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 7:00pm MST /8:00pm MDT/ the stage was 18.06 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest near 18 feet is expected at 8:00pm MST /9:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Leupp, Birdsprings, Bushman Acres, Homolovi Ruins State Park.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of rivers are unstable and
unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 23 at 4:16PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A series of fronts are expected to move across the Interior on
Sunday and Monday. The initial front on Sunday will bring a band
of snowfall across the area. With this first front, light snow
accumulations are expected.

The next front moving across the Interior on Monday will be
accompanied by warmer temperatures, which could bring the
potential for a light rain/snow mix in the valleys and moderate
snow amounts across higher elevations. This could lead to slick
travel conditions, especially during the overnight hours Monday
night into Tuesday when the temperatures could drop below freezing
once again.

Accompanying the second front will be a period of gusty winds
across the higher elevations. This could bring some blowing snow
concerns Monday night/Tuesday morning, which could reduce
visibility to one mile or less.

Stay up to date with the latest forecast by visiting our website,
weather.gov/afg.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Nassau; Coastal Glynn; Coastal Camden
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 23 at 7:33PM EDT until October 26 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7-11 ft.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM to 5 PM EDT
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 8 AM Saturday to 8
PM EDT Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 5 PM
Saturday to 8 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 9:15AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
30W was upgraded to Tropical Storm In-fa over the northern Marshall
Islands at 700 AM ChST this morning, located near 10.6N 166.3E, or
120 miles north-northeast of Ujae Atoll, south of Bikini and Rongelap
Atolls. In-fa has maximum sustained winds of 40 mph, which extend
outward 115 miles to the southeast, 105 miles to the southwest, 100
miles to the northwest, and 40 miles to the northeast. This keeps
Ujae Atoll just outside the direct tropical storm-force wind field,
but strong sustained west to southwest winds with damaging tropical
storm-force gusts are expected through at least tonight as In-fa
begins to meander generally northward. The worst impacts will be
felt for islands and atolls across the northern and central Marshall
Islands, especially for west-facing exposures along the Ralik Chain,
such as Ujae, Enewetak, and Kwajalein Atolls. To the south of In-fa,
expect surging west to southwest winds of 20 to 30 knots with gusts
up to 45 knots, especially near heavier showers or outflow
boundaries. Boats should be safely secured away from west or south-
facing exposures, if possible. Significant boat damage has been
reported along west reefs already.

Seas will be hazardous to small craft throughout much of the central
and northern RMI, and dangerous within the tropical storm-force
winds closer to the center of In-fa. Do not attempt inter-island
travel. Even within the relatively calmer lagoon-side waters, inter-
island travel is strongly discouraged. Passing showers may produce
sudden strong to gale-force gusts, which will create locally
dangerous conditions. West to southwest swells will build to the
south of In- fa through the rest of the weekend, leading to elevated,
potentially hazardous surf along west- and south-facing reefs of the
central and northern RMI, mainly to the north and northwest of
Majuro.

Currently, In-fa is nearly-stationary, with its recent motion showing
a slight southeastward drift at around 1 mph, but is forecast to
begin slowly meandering north-northeast, then north-northwest through
this afternoon. Then, In-fa will see a slight increase in forward
speed through Sunday as it begins to exit the Marshall Islands. Winds
and seas will begin to ease through Sunday night, but sea conditions
may remain hazardous to small craft across the northern Marshalls
through Monday night. Light winds and a drier ridging pattern look to
set up across the region by the end of the week. This situation
will be closely monitored for additional impacts to the Marshall
Islands.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header
WTPQ31 PGUM.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 12:26PM AKDT until October 25 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Water levels of 4 to
6.5 feet above the normal high tide line expected.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...For Nome and Golovin, water levels are
expected to rise to around 6 feet above the normal high tide
line. In Nome, this can result in water approaching low-lying
homes in Belmont Subdivision with standing water expected in
the port area. For Golovin, water may inundate any beach
property but the roads, buildings and residences shouldn't be
impacted as the water remains below the berm. Water levels
will peak Friday afternoon and gradually drop, but remain
above normal through the weekend.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is possible
in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...From 9 AM Monday to 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 11:39 AM
Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43
PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up to 1.0 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat.High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 12:25PM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches, Santa Barbara County Southwestern
Coast, Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and
harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea water
inundation is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(around 1.1 to 1.5 feet above astronomical projections) Sunday-
Thursday, peaking Monday-Wednesday. High tides will peak in the
morning hours. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal
Flood Warnings (highest chances Wednesday-Thursday) if larger
surf develops.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 11:31AM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

San Juan River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Farmington.

* WHEN...From this morning to Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.5 feet, Overbank flow is occurring from just below
the confluence of the Animas and San Juan Rivers at Farmington, and
continuing downriver through Shiprock. At this water level, the
fast flow can result in river bank erosion but otherwise minor
flood damage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 5.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.2 feet
late tomorrow evening.
- Action stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.
